title: Reversible shared block with Mirror depth views
hypothesis: A shared reversible additive-coupling block with a scalar Mirror coordinate at each depth step retains synthetic task quality while reducing saved activation memory and parameter bytes with bounded recomputation cost.
physical_object: one shared additive-coupling block repeated eight times
mirror_coordinate: one learned scalar per repeated depth step modulating coupling branches
logical_multiplicity: eight distinct depth-step functions from shared block parameters
controls: reversible tied block with Mirror scalar views

development.selection_metric: task MSE, serialized weight bytes, peak saved activation bytes, MAC proxy, wall time

success_gate: Both dev worlds: Mirror MSE within 5% of untied upper control, >=30% lower saved activation bytes than ordinary tied unrolled, >=10% fewer parameter bytes than untied, runtime <=2x tied; direct gate >=10% larger or worse quality for Mirror-specific claim.
failure_gate: Quality or activation-saving threshold missed, runtime >2x, or direct gate within 10%; fresh sealed.
boundaries: no Transformer or GPU scaling claim
activation memory and recomputation are reported separately
